learn.hook: A butterfly, a rangoli and the Taj Mahal share a secret: their parts repeat in a perfect pattern!
points: Symmetry means parts of a figure repeat in a definite pattern.
In mirror symmetry, one half is the mirror image of the other, like a butterfly's wings.
In turning symmetry, a part repeats as you turn around a centre, like the petals of a flower or the pattern of a rangoli.
Symmetry is everywhere in nature (leaves, butterflies, snowflakes), art (rangoli, kolam) and buildings (the Taj Mahal, temple gopurams).

example.q: Why do we say the front of the Taj Mahal is symmetric?
steps: Imagine a vertical line through the middle of the main dome.
The left half (minarets, arches) matches the right half exactly, like a mirror image.
So its parts repeat in a definite pattern: it has symmetry.
example.answer: Its left and right halves are mirror images

learn.reallife: Designers use symmetry in sarees, logos and jewellery because our eyes find it balanced and beautiful.

games.title: Is it symmetric?
items: Its wings match across the body.
Symmetry means parts repeat in a definite pattern.
That is the idea of symmetry.
A rangoli can have turning symmetry.
Its pattern repeats as you turn it.
Its parts don't repeat in a pattern.

quiz.q: What does symmetry mean?
options: Parts of a figure repeat in a definite pattern
quiz.explain: Symmetry is about parts repeating in a pattern.
quiz.mistake: Thinks symmetry means neatness

quiz.q: Which has mirror (line) symmetry?
quiz.explain: A butterfly's left and right wings match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks irregular objects are symmetric

quiz.q: Which is a famous symmetric building in India?
quiz.explain: Its front is a mirror image across the middle.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect buildings with symmetry

quiz.q: A flower with 6 identical petals looks the same after turning. What kind of symmetry is this?
quiz.explain: Its petals repeat as you turn it about the centre.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only mirror symmetry exists

quiz.q: Where is symmetry often seen in Indian art?
quiz.explain: Rangoli and kolam patterns repeat beautifully.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice symmetry in art

quiz.q: A temple gopuram has carvings that are the same on the left and right of its centre. This shows…
quiz.explain: Left matches right across a vertical middle line.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two types

quiz.q: Which natural object usually shows symmetry?
quiz.explain: Most leaves are nearly the same on both sides of the middle vein.
quiz.mistake: Thinks nature has no symmetry

quiz.q: Which of these does NOT show symmetry?
quiz.explain: Crumpled paper has no repeating pattern.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every object has symmetry

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What makes a butterfly symmetric?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Its two halves match like mirror images. That's symmetry!
teach.nudge: What do you notice about the left and right wings?

learn.hook: Fold a butterfly picture down the middle and both wings match perfectly. That's line symmetry!
points: A shape has line symmetry if you can fold it along a line so that the two halves match exactly.
The fold line is called the line of symmetry (or axis of symmetry). Each half is a mirror image of the other.
Some shapes have many lines of symmetry: a rectangle has 2, an equilateral triangle 3, a square 4 and a circle has unlimited lines.
A regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry. A regular hexagon has 6.
Capital letters: A and M have a vertical line, B and E a horizontal line, H and X have both, and F, G, J and R have none.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
steps: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides.
Each line of symmetry goes through one corner and the middle of the opposite side.
There are 5 corners, so 5 lines.

learn.reallife: The Taj Mahal, rangoli designs, leaves and many temple doors are symmetrical.

games.title: How many lines of symmetry? (capital letters)
Match the shape to its lines of symmetry

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square has 2 lines through the middles of opposite sides and 2 along its diagonals: 4 in all.
steps: Vertical + horizontal = 2
Two diagonals = 2
Total = 4
quiz.mistake: Forgets the diagonal lines (2)

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: Only the vertical and horizontal middle lines work. Folding along a diagonal does not make the halves match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry

quiz.q: Which capital letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: R has a leg on one side only, so no fold makes its halves match. A and T have a vertical line; H has two lines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a letter looks balanced, so it must be symmetrical

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon have?
quiz.explain: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as sides. An octagon has 8 sides, so 8 lines.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the lines through corners (4) or doubles (16)

quiz.q: Riya folds a paper and cuts half a heart shape along the fold. When she opens it, what is the fold line?
quiz.explain: Both halves of the heart were cut together, so they match exactly across the fold.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect folding with symmetry

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
quiz.explain: Each line goes from a corner to the middle of the opposite side. There are 3 corners, so 3 lines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of only the vertical line (1)

quiz.q: Written in capital letters, which word looks exactly the same after folding along a horizontal line through its middle?
quiz.explain: B, O and X each have a horizontal line of symmetry. A, M, P and T do not.
quiz.mistake: Checks for a vertical line instead of a horizontal one

quiz.q: Arjun says a circle has exactly 4 lines of symmetry. Is he right?
options: No, every line through the centre is a line of symmetry
quiz.explain: Any fold through the centre of a circle makes two matching halves, so it has unlimited lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the vertical, horizontal and diagonal lines

teach.ask: Gappu looks at a butterfly: 'People say it's symmetrical. What does that mean?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Fold it on the line of symmetry and both halves match like a mirror. Butterflies are so neat!
teach.nudge: What happens to the two halves when I fold along the middle?

learn.hook: Put a mirror on the line and the picture completes itself!
points: In reflection symmetry each point has a mirror image on the other side of the line, at the same distance from it.
A point 3 squares to the left of a vertical line of symmetry has its image 3 squares to the right, in the same row.
Not every fold is a line of symmetry: a diagonal of a non-square rectangle is NOT a line of symmetry, because the folded triangles don't sit exactly on each other.
To complete a figure on squared paper, reflect each corner point across the line, then join the image points in the same order.

example.q: On squared paper, the line of symmetry is vertical. Point P is 2 squares left of it and 4 squares up. Where is its image?
steps: Stay in the same row: 4 squares up.
Go to the other side, the same distance: 2 squares right of the line.
The image is 2 right of the line, 4 up.

learn.reallife: Lakes reflect mountains, and a dressing mirror shows your mirror image: same distance behind the mirror as you are in front.

games.title: Reflection facts
items: The image of a point is the same distance from the line on the other side.
A rectangle's diagonal is a line of symmetry.
The halves don't match when folded.
A square's diagonal is a line of symmetry.
Reflecting a point across a vertical line changes its row.
To complete a figure, reflect its corners and join them in order.

games.title: Find the image (vertical line of symmetry)

quiz.q: A point is 5 squares to the left of a vertical line of symmetry. Where is its image?
quiz.explain: The image is the same distance on the other side.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the distance

quiz.q: Why is the diagonal of a 6 cm × 3 cm rectangle not a line of symmetry?
options: Folding along it, the two triangles don't sit exactly on each other
quiz.explain: Folding along the diagonal leaves corners sticking out.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every line that cuts a shape in two equal halves is a line of symmetry

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a 6 cm × 3 cm rectangle have?
quiz.explain: Only the two lines through the midpoints of opposite sides.
quiz.mistake: Counts the diagonals too

quiz.q: A point is ON the line of symmetry. Where is its image?
options: On the other side of the paper
quiz.explain: Its distance from the line is 0, so it is its own image.
quiz.mistake: Moves it anyway

quiz.q: The line of symmetry is horizontal. Point Q is 3 squares above it. Where is the image?
options: 3 squares below it, in the same column
quiz.explain: Across a horizontal line, the image goes down the same distance.
quiz.mistake: Moves sideways instead

quiz.q: Shreya completes half a kite on squared paper. The top corner is on the line and the side corner is 3 squares left of it. How wide is the full kite?
quiz.explain: The side corner's image is 3 right, so the width is 3 + 3 = 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Gives only half the width

quiz.q: In a mirror, Vikram stands 2 m in front of the glass. How far is his image from him?
quiz.explain: The image is 2 m behind the mirror, so 2 + 2 = 4 m from him.
quiz.mistake: Gives the distance to the mirror

quiz.q: Which line is a line of symmetry of a square?
options: A line joining two neighbouring corners
A line from a corner to the middle of a far side
quiz.explain: Folding a square along a diagonal makes the halves match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only vertical lines work

teach.ask: Gappu folds his rectangular leaf corner to corner. 'Do the halves match?'
teach.praise: Chirp! For a long rectangle the diagonal fold doesn't match: corners stick out!
teach.nudge: What do you see sticking out after the fold?

topics.title: Making symmetric shapes: blots, folds and cuts

learn.hook: Drop ink, fold, press, open: you've made a perfect butterfly!
points: Ink blot: put a few drops of paint on one side of a fold, press the paper, open it: the blot is symmetric about the fold.
Fold and cut: cut a shape along a folded edge, and the opened shape is symmetric about the fold line.
Punching a hole through a folded paper makes two holes, mirror images across the fold.
Folding twice (in half, then in half again) and cutting gives a shape with 2 lines of symmetry. A hole punched through gives 4 holes.
To predict the result, imagine unfolding step by step, reflecting the cut each time.

example.q: A paper is folded in half twice. A hole is punched once through all layers. How many holes appear when opened?
steps: The first fold makes 2 layers; the second makes 4 layers.
One punch goes through 4 layers.
So 4 holes appear, arranged symmetrically.

learn.reallife: Paper doilies, Diwali paper lanterns and garlands of paper dolls are made by folding and cutting.

items.q: Layers after folding in half twice

games.title: Predict the shape
items: Cutting a half-circle on the fold gives a full circle.
The fold makes the other half.
An ink blot pressed on a fold is symmetric about the fold.
The paint prints its mirror image.
Folding once and punching once gives 1 hole.
Cutting a triangle on the fold of a folded paper can give a rhombus or kite shape.
The two halves join at the fold.
A double fold and one cut gives a shape with 2 lines of symmetry.
Each fold line is a line of symmetry.

quiz.q: Paper is folded once and a hole punched through it. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: Two layers, so two holes, mirror images across the fold.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the hidden layer

quiz.q: Paper is folded in half 3 times and punched once. How many holes?
quiz.explain: Each fold doubles the layers: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of doubling

quiz.q: A half-circle is cut along the fold of a folded sheet. What shape is the hole?
quiz.explain: The fold gives the other half: a full circle.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the mirror half

quiz.q: Rina puts a blob of paint on one side of a fold and presses. What does she see when she opens it?
options: A shape symmetric about the fold
quiz.explain: Pressing copies the blob as its mirror image.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the print is random

quiz.q: A paper is folded in half twice (into quarters) and a corner at the centre point is cut off. What is the hole like?
options: A shape with 2 lines of symmetry in the middle
A hole at one edge only
Four separate holes at the corners
quiz.explain: The centre corner of all four layers is cut, giving one hole with both fold lines as lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it makes four separate holes

quiz.q: A paper is folded once and then punched twice. How many holes appear when it is opened?
quiz.explain: Each punch makes 2 holes: 2 × 2 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the punches

quiz.q: A row of paper dolls is cut from a strip folded zig-zag into 4 layers. How many dolls appear?
quiz.explain: Each layer gives one doll: 4 dolls.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each fold gives one doll

quiz.q: Which fold line is the line of symmetry of an ink-blot butterfly?
quiz.explain: The blot is printed as a mirror image across the fold.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a different line is the axis

teach.ask: Gappu folds a leaf twice and makes one hole. 'How many holes will I see?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Two folds make 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes!
teach.nudge: How many layers does the punch go through?

learn.hook: Some triangles have 3 lines of symmetry, some have 1, and some have none!
points: An equilateral triangle (all sides equal) has 3 lines of symmetry: from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
An isosceles triangle (exactly two sides equal) has 1 line of symmetry: from the corner between the equal sides to the middle of the opposite side.
A scalene triangle (all sides different) has no line of symmetry.
A regular hexagon has 6 lines of symmetry: 3 through opposite corners and 3 through the middles of opposite sides.

example.q: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
steps: Two sides are equal (5 cm), the third is different.
So it is isosceles.
It has 1 line of symmetry, from the corner between the 5 cm sides to the middle of the 8 cm side.

learn.reallife: Roof trusses are often isosceles triangles, and road warning signs are equilateral triangles: balanced and symmetric.

games.title: Lines of symmetry
items: Isosceles triangle with a 30° top angle

games.title: Shape and its lines of symmetry

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with sides 7 cm, 7 cm, 7 cm have?
quiz.explain: It is equilateral, so it has 3 lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with sides 6 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm have?
quiz.explain: It is isosceles: 1 line through the corner between the equal sides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all triangles have 3

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 cm have?
quiz.explain: All sides differ (scalene), so no line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Assumes every triangle has one

quiz.q: Where is the line of symmetry of an isosceles triangle?
options: Along one of the equal sides
From the middle of an equal side to the opposite corner
From the corner between the equal sides to the middle of the opposite side
quiz.explain: Folding there makes the two equal sides lie on each other.
quiz.mistake: Picks a line along a side

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
quiz.explain: 3 through opposite corners and 3 through the middles of opposite sides.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the corner-to-corner lines

quiz.q: A triangle has exactly one line of symmetry. What can it be?
quiz.explain: Exactly one line means exactly two equal sides.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the triangle types

quiz.q: Can a triangle have exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: If it has two, it must have three equal sides and so 3 lines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any number is possible

quiz.q: A road sign is an equilateral triangle. How many ways can it be folded so the halves match?
quiz.explain: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the vertical fold

teach.ask: Gappu has a triangle with sides 4, 4 and 6. 'How many ways can I fold it so halves match?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Two equal sides make it isosceles: just 1 line of symmetry!
teach.nudge: How many of its sides are equal?

learn.hook: Spin a pinwheel a little and it looks just the same. That's rotational symmetry!
points: A shape has rotational symmetry if it looks exactly the same after a turn of less than a full turn about its centre.
The smallest such turn is the smallest angle of symmetry. For a square it is 90°.
A square matches itself at 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°: 4 times in one full turn.
Smallest angle × number of matches = 360°. For an equilateral triangle: 120° × 3 = 360°.
The Ashoka Chakra on our flag has 24 equal spokes, so its smallest angle of symmetry is 360° ÷ 24 = 15°.

example.q: A pinwheel has 4 identical blades. What is its smallest angle of rotational symmetry?
steps: The blades are evenly spaced around a full turn of 360°.
There are 4 blades.

learn.reallife: Ceiling fans, bicycle wheels, flowers and many rangoli patterns have rotational symmetry.

games.title: Match the shape to its smallest angle of symmetry

items.q: Smallest angle of symmetry: flower with 6 identical petals
Smallest angle of symmetry: wheel with 8 evenly spaced spokes
Smallest angle of symmetry: fan with 3 identical blades
Smallest angle of symmetry: Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes)
How many times does a square match itself in one full turn?
Smallest angle is 30°. How many matches in a full turn?

quiz.q: What is the smallest angle of rotational symmetry of a square?
quiz.explain: A square looks the same after a quarter turn: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.
steps: 4 matching positions
quiz.mistake: Thinks of a half turn (180°) or confuses with the diagonal angle (45°)

quiz.q: A ceiling fan has 3 identical, evenly spaced blades. What is the smallest turn that makes it look the same?
steps: 3 blades
quiz.mistake: Uses 90° out of habit, as for a square

quiz.q: A rangoli looks the same after every turn of 45°. How many times does it match itself in one full turn?
quiz.explain: 360° ÷ 45° = 8 matches in a full turn.
quiz.mistake: Writes the angle itself (45) or halves the answer (4)

quiz.q: Which shape looks the same after a 180° turn but NOT after a 90° turn?
options: A rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: A rectangle swaps its long and short sides after 90°, so it doesn't match, but after 180° it does.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a square matches at 90° too

quiz.q: A regular hexagon is turned about its centre. What is the smallest angle that makes it look the same?
quiz.explain: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3 (120°) or by 12 (30°)

quiz.q: Kabir's bicycle wheel has 12 identical, evenly spaced spokes. What is its smallest angle of symmetry?
quiz.mistake: Uses the number of spokes as the angle (12°)

quiz.q: Which of these has NO rotational symmetry (except a full turn)?
quiz.explain: F looks different after any turn less than 360°. S looks the same after a half turn (180°).
quiz.mistake: Thinks S has no symmetry because it has no line of symmetry

quiz.q: Joseph says every shape with a line of symmetry also has rotational symmetry. Is he right?
options: No: the letter A has a line of symmetry but no rotational symmetry
quiz.explain: Fold A down the middle and the halves match, but turn A and it looks different until a full turn.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up line symmetry and rotational symmetry

quiz.q: After its first step, the Koch snowflake looks like a six-pointed star. What is its smallest angle of rotational symmetry?
quiz.explain: The star has 6 identical points, so it matches itself every 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. Its order of rotational symmetry is 6.
steps: 6 identical points
quiz.mistake: Uses the 3 sides of the starting triangle

teach.ask: Gappu spins a flower with 5 petals: 'What is rotational symmetry, and how do I find its angle?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Turn it until it looks the same again: 360° ÷ 5 = 72°. My flower has rotational symmetry!
teach.nudge: How far do I turn it before it looks the same, and how do I work that angle out?

topics.title: Centre of rotation and angles of symmetry

learn.hook: A pinwheel spins around one fixed point. That point is the secret to its symmetry!
points: The centre of rotation is the fixed point a figure turns about.
For figures with radial arms (like spokes or fan blades), the arrangement of the arms decides the angles of symmetry. 4 equally spaced arms → 90°, 180°, 270°, 360°.
If arms are not equally spaced, the figure may only match at 360°: arms pointing up, right and down (no left arm) match only after a full turn.
All angles of symmetry are multiples of the smallest one, and the smallest one divides 360° exactly.
So a figure can't have a smallest angle of symmetry of 70°, because 70 does not divide 360.

example.q: A figure has 5 identical, equally spaced arms. List its angles of symmetry.
steps: Smallest angle = 360° ÷ 5 = 72°.
Order of rotational symmetry = 5.

learn.reallife: A wheel turns about its axle (the centre of rotation), and fan blades spread evenly so the fan looks the same as it spins.

items.q: Second angle of symmetry: 6 equal arms
Order if the smallest angle is 45°
Order if the smallest angle is 120°

games.title: Can it be?
items: A smallest angle of symmetry of 60° is possible.
A smallest angle of symmetry of 70° is possible.
If 90° is an angle of symmetry, so is 180°.
Three arms pointing up, right and down have a 90° angle of symmetry.
After 90° there is no arm pointing left to match.
The centre of rotation stays fixed during the turn.

quiz.q: A wheel has 10 equally spaced spokes. What is its smallest angle of symmetry?
quiz.mistake: Uses the number of spokes as the angle

quiz.q: A figure's smallest angle of symmetry is 60°. Which of these is also an angle of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Angles of symmetry are multiples of 60°: 120°, 180°, 240°, 300°, 360°.
quiz.mistake: Picks any angle bigger than 60°

quiz.q: Which can NOT be the smallest angle of symmetry of a figure?
quiz.explain: 360 ÷ 50 is not a whole number, so 50° can't be the smallest angle.
quiz.mistake: Does not check if it divides 360

quiz.q: A figure has arms pointing up, right and down only (equal lengths). What is its order of rotational symmetry?
quiz.explain: Turning 90° or 180° moves an arm to the empty left side. It matches only after 360°: order 1.
quiz.mistake: Counts arms instead of checking turns

quiz.q: Where is the centre of rotation of a ceiling fan?
options: At the middle where the blades join
quiz.explain: The blades turn about the middle point.
quiz.mistake: Picks a point that moves

quiz.q: A rangoli has 8 equal petals. How many angles of symmetry does it have in a full turn (including 360°)?
quiz.explain: Smallest angle 45°, and 360 ÷ 45 = 8 angles.
quiz.mistake: Gives the angle instead of the count

quiz.q: A figure has angles of symmetry 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°. What is the smallest?
quiz.explain: The smallest angle of symmetry is 90°, and the others are its multiples.
quiz.mistake: Picks the largest

quiz.q: A logo has 3 identical arms spaced 120° apart. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a 3-armed figure has order 6

teach.ask: Gappu sees a star with 6 equal points. 'Which turns make it look the same?'

topics.title: Circles, coloured sectors and tile designs

learn.hook: A circle is the champion of symmetry: it matches itself after ANY turn!
points: A circle looks the same after a turn of any angle about its centre, and every diameter is a line of symmetry.
Colouring sectors can control the order: a circle cut into 8 equal sectors with every other sector coloured has order 4 (it matches every 90°).
With 8 sectors, colouring two opposite sectors (like 1 and 5) gives order 2; colouring just one gives order 1.
Tile designs: arrange square tiles with patterns to get exactly one or exactly two lines of symmetry. Check each possible fold line one by one.

example.q: A circle is cut into 6 equal sectors. Sectors 1 and 4 are coloured. What is the order of rotational symmetry?
steps: The coloured sectors are opposite each other (3 apart).
A half turn (180°) moves sector 1 to 4 and 4 to 1: the same look.
A 60° or 120° turn does not match, so the order is 2.

learn.reallife: Wheels, coins and plates are round so they look and work the same however they are turned.

games.title: Order of the coloured circle (8 equal sectors)
Circle facts
items: Every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry.
Folding along it matches the halves.
A circle has exactly 4 lines of symmetry.
A circle looks the same after a 37° turn.
Any turn works for a circle.
Colouring every other sector of 8 gives order 2.
A tile design can have exactly one line of symmetry.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
quiz.explain: Every diameter is a line of symmetry, and there are endlessly many diameters.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer is 4 like a square

quiz.q: Which turn makes a circle look the same?
quiz.explain: Every angle is an angle of symmetry of a circle.
quiz.mistake: Applies a polygon's rule

quiz.q: A circle has 8 equal sectors; sectors 1, 3, 5, 7 are coloured. What is the order of rotational symmetry?
quiz.explain: A 90° turn shifts by 2 sectors and keeps the pattern. 360 ÷ 90 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks colouring half gives order 2

quiz.q: A circle has 8 equal sectors; only sectors 1 and 5 are coloured. What is the order?
quiz.explain: Only a 180° (or 360°) turn keeps the pattern: order 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two coloured parts means order 4

quiz.q: A circle has 6 equal sectors. Which colouring gives order 3?
quiz.explain: Colouring every other sector matches every 120°: 360 ÷ 120 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks opposite sectors (order 2)

quiz.q: A circle has 12 equal sectors with sectors 1, 5 and 9 coloured. What is the smallest angle of symmetry?
quiz.explain: The coloured sectors are 4 apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.
quiz.mistake: Uses one sector's angle

quiz.q: A 2 × 2 tile design has two plain tiles on the left and two tiles with vertical stripes on the right. How many lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Only the horizontal middle line works; left and right differ.
quiz.mistake: Counts the vertical line too

quiz.q: A 2 × 2 design has plain tiles at top-left and bottom-right, and tiles with vertical stripes at the other two corners. Which turn keeps it the same?
quiz.explain: A half turn swaps top-left with bottom-right and top-right with bottom-left, keeping the pattern.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a quarter turn works

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Can I turn a circle by any angle and it still looks the same?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Yes! Any turn about the centre, and every diameter is a line of symmetry!
teach.nudge: Is there any turn that changes how a circle looks?

learn.hook: Two players, one grid, dominoes. Copy your opponent the clever way and you can't lose!
points: Game: on a grid, players take turns covering two neighbouring squares (a domino). The player who cannot move loses.
Symmetry strategy: on a 4 × 4 grid, the second player answers each move with the move you get by a half turn (180°) about the centre of the grid.
The copied squares are always empty, because the grid looks the same after a half turn, and no domino on a 4 × 4 grid can be its own copy. So the second player always has a move and wins.
Figures can have line symmetry only (letter A), rotational symmetry only (letter S, letter N), both (letter H, a square) or neither (letter F).

example.q: On a 4 × 4 grid, the first player covers the first two squares of the top row (top-left corner). Where should the second player play?
steps: A half turn about the centre sends the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner.
So copy the domino onto the last two squares of the bottom row (bottom-right corner).
Keep copying like this after every move.
example.answer: The last two squares of the bottom row

learn.reallife: Chess and carrom players also use symmetry ideas to plan clever replies.

games.title: Game strategy
items: In the half-turn strategy, the second player copies the move turned 180° about the centre.
The copied squares might already be covered.
The board is symmetric before each move, and a domino never overlaps its own half-turn copy, so the copy squares are empty.
The letter S has rotational symmetry.
It looks the same after a half turn.
The letter A has rotational symmetry of order 2.
A square has both line and rotational symmetry.

quiz.q: Which letter has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: S looks the same after a half turn but has no fold line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks S has a line of symmetry

quiz.q: Which letter has both line and rotational symmetry?
quiz.explain: H has a vertical and a horizontal line and matches after 180°.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter with only one type

quiz.q: Which letter has neither line nor rotational symmetry?
quiz.explain: F has no fold line and doesn't match after any part turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Z has no symmetry (it has rotation)

quiz.q: In the 4 × 4 domino game, the first player covers two squares in the top row, 2nd and 3rd from the left. Where does the half-turn copy go?
options: Bottom row, 2nd and 3rd from the left
quiz.explain: A half turn sends the top row to the bottom row, and the middle pair stays in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Copies across a line instead of turning

quiz.q: Why does the half-turn strategy always give the second player a move?
options: The board is symmetric after each pair of moves, so the copy squares are free
The first player always makes mistakes
quiz.explain: After every copy the covered squares are symmetric, so the half-turn copy of a new move lands on empty squares. A domino can never overlap its own copy, because the grid has no centre square.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the role of symmetry

quiz.q: Who wins the 4 × 4 domino game if the second player uses the half-turn strategy?
quiz.explain: The second player always has a reply, so the first player runs out of moves first.
quiz.mistake: Assumes the first player has the advantage

quiz.q: A shape has line symmetry but no rotational symmetry. Which could it be?
quiz.explain: A has a vertical line of symmetry but turned 180° it looks different.
quiz.mistake: Thinks line symmetry always comes with rotation

quiz.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of the letter N?
quiz.explain: N matches after 180° and 360°: order 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks N has no rotational symmetry

teach.ask: Gappu plays the domino game second on a 4 × 4 grid. 'How can I always win?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Copy every move with a half turn about the centre. Gappu wins!
teach.nudge: How can you use the centre of the grid to answer each move?
